overview: Mali's women's health landscape is shaped less by venture-backed femtech startups than by government, donor, and NGO programs tackling one of the world's highest maternal mortality ratios (440 per 100,000). The most consequential innovation is DISC-Mali, a national digital community health system built on the open-source Community Health Toolkit that equips tens of thousands of community health workers to track pregnancies and maternal care. Alongside it, a 2025-2029 budgeted family planning plan, a 2024-2028 national digital health strategy, and a Global Fund-backed free maternal care financing pilot anchor the ecosystem, while conflict and 2025 aid funding cuts strain reproductive health services in the north and center.

sections.heading: Latest major news
sections.narrative: Recent developments center on government-donor financing reforms for free maternal care and the strain of conflict and funding cuts on reproductive health services.

items.text: Mali's Ministry of Health and Muso signed an MoU making Muso the independent verification agent for a new Global Fund-backed Direct Health Facility Financing (DHFF) pilot for free maternal and newborn care.
DHFF free-care pilot launched across 53 community health centers (37 in Kayes, 16 in Bamako); prenatal consultations rose sharply for pregnant women covered up to 42 days postpartum.
Intensifying conflict in Timbuktu, Gao, Mopti and Menaka pushed internal displacement toward 380,000; under 25% of health facilities in crisis regions offer comprehensive SRH or GBV care.
UNFPA warned that global funding cuts to midwifery support put the lives of pregnant women and newborns at risk, with Mali among the affected countries.

sections.heading: Policy & strategy
sections.narrative: Mali has adopted overlapping national strategies covering family planning, digital health, and community health digitization.

items.text: Government launched the Budgeted National Action Plan (PANB) 2025-2029 for family planning, aiming to raise modern contraceptive prevalence from 21% toward 30%, with ~81.4 billion FCFA budgeted (42% for contraceptive commodities).

Adoption of the 2024-2028 National Digital Health Strategic Plan (PSNSN), backed by a projected USD 35M budget, prioritizing telemedicine, interoperability and a national health database with UNICEF, World Bank, UNDP, USAID and WHO.

Ministry of Health launched DISC-Mali (Digitalisation de la Sante Communautaire), a Community Health Toolkit-based system to reach national scale by 2025 and equip 25,000+ health workers, built with MUSO, UNICEF, Medic and Keneya Neita.
Ministry of Health and Social Development launched a national digital health information portal centralizing ministry services, advancing the PSNSN strategy.

sections.heading: Latest ecosystem moves
sections.narrative: Ecosystem activity is dominated by digital community health deployment and menstrual health programming, supported by a small local incubator scene.

items.text: DISC-Mali scaling nationwide: community health workers record pregnancy and maternal data on smartphones, with appointment reminders and real-time reporting via the open-source Community Health Toolkit.
UNICEF menstrual health programming trained 510 people (including 264 girls) to make reusable pads in schools, with plans to scale nationally toward 2.5M+ students.
CECI distributed menstrual hygiene kits to adolescent girls across several Malian high schools.
UNFPA supported mobile midwife/nurse teams and, in 2023, trained 50+ midwives in Mopti and renovated 12 rural maternity wards to sustain SRH access in conflict zones.
Bamako incubators (Impact Hub Bamako, DoniLab, CREATeam, Jokkolabs, Teteliso) form the local startup-support base, though focus skews to agribusiness and general tech over dedicated femtech.

sections.heading: Notable funding rounds
sections.narrative: Financing in Mali's women's-health space is program and donor grants rather than startup equity rounds.

sections.heading: Key players & hubs
sections.narrative: The core actors are government bodies, global-health NGOs, and open-source digital health partners, plus Bamako's incubator network.

items.name: Muso Health
items.note: Founded 2005; proactive community case management reaching 330,000+ patients; verification agent for the DHFF free maternal care pilot.

items.name: DISC-Mali (Ministry of Health digital community health system)
items.note: National Community Health Toolkit deployment for pregnancy tracking and maternal care by community health workers.

items.name: Medic
items.note: Nonprofit behind the open-source Community Health Toolkit powering DISC-Mali's maternal and newborn health workflows.

items.name: Mali Health
items.note: Bamako-based organization improving maternal and child health via community health systems and quality improvement.

items.name: ONASR (National Office of Sexual & Reproductive Health)
items.note: Initiated the Bangue Bamu integrated maternal-neonatal telemedicine platform feasibility study with AGEFAU.

items.name: UNFPA Mali
items.note: Active since 1973; distributes reproductive health supplies, funds midwife training and mobile SRH teams in conflict areas.

items.name: UNICEF Mali
items.note: Runs school menstrual health and hygiene programs and co-funds the digital health strategy.

items.name: Impact Hub Bamako
items.note: First Impact Hub in Francophone Africa; supports young and women entrepreneurs in Bamako's ACI 2000 district.

items.name: DoniLab
items.note: Bamako incubator, Afric'innov-certified, part of the local hackathon and startup-support network.

sections.heading: Active investors
sections.narrative: Funders are almost entirely development donors and global-health financiers rather than gender-lens venture funds.

items.name: The Global Fund
items.role: Backs the DHFF results-based free maternal and newborn care pilot.

items.name: World Bank
items.role: Partner and funder of the national digital health strategy.

items.name: USAID
items.role: Supporting partner for the digital health strategy (pre-2025 aid landscape).

items.name: UNDP
items.role: Supports digital health (SanDi community health worker training) and Pan-African HealthTech via timbuktoo.

items.name: UNICEF
items.role: Co-funds DISC-Mali digital community health and menstrual health programs.

items.name: Ouagadougou Partnership
items.role: Regional family planning financing and coordination platform including Mali.
